newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swap - Gas oil up on physical push.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swap - Gas oil up on physical push.

text.p: Singapore gas oil and jet fuel swaps firmed at midday on Thursday on renewed physical buying interest after a lapse of a few weeks during which prices sank to a near three-year low, traders said.
"Gas oil picked up after yesterday's deal," one trader said.
But players cautious of the rally due to the high stocks of middle distillate in Singapore amid poor regional demand.
August swaps were indicated at $21.65/$21.75 per barrel, up from Tuesday's $21.35/$21.45. August was traded in the morning at $21.70 per barrel, brokers said.
Traders said current sentiment is similar to that seen early Wednesday when August was traded up to a high of $21.75 before ending weaker late in the evening.
The swaps were also held up by trading firms and banks who were playing the East-West spread by buying the East and selling the West, they said.
In the physical market a 150,000-barrel cargo traded on Wednesday at $20.60 per barrel, free-on-board Singapore, up 80 cents from the lowest offered level last week.
The deal is the first in over two weeks.
Jet fuel also traded on at a higher level on renewed buying interest with a 100,000 barrel cargo traded at $23.50, well above the $22.10 last trade done on July 9.

As a result the regrade has firmed even though outright gas oil swaps values have also risen sharply. August regrade traded late Wednesday at $1.95 per barrel compared to an early week deal at $1.60, brokers said.
August regrade was last quoted notionally at $1.80/$2.00 per barrel, they said.
Fuel oil swaps were steady with August and September last quoted unchanged at $97.50/$98.50.
